## earnings / 03_margin-drivers.md

_Source: `earnings/03_margin-drivers.md`_

# Margin Drivers — NU

NU reports under IFRS Accounting Standards in U.S. dollars. Amounts below are US$ millions unless noted. The primary margin read uses Nu's lender metrics: net interest margin (NIM), risk-adjusted NIM (NIM after management's cost-of-credit measure), funding cost, and operating efficiency. NIM and risk-adjusted NIM are annualized management measures, not IFRS line items.

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

**Sector overlay applied: bank / lender — margin analysis uses NIM, risk-adjusted NIM, credit cost, and efficiency ratio.** Nu has one reportable segment, Nu Group, representing 100% of disclosed revenue and profit. It does not disclose country, product, or segment profit; the analysis is therefore consolidated. Brazil is economically concentrated but is not a reportable profit segment. [FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 34, F-97–F-98]

The strict cost-to-income ratio and a CASA split are not disclosed. Nu instead reports an efficiency ratio: total operating expenses divided by NII plus fee income net of transactional cost and revenue-based taxes. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slides 6 and 22]

Capital IQ's FY2025 banking line is US$6,991m (100% of its vendor-defined segment total), not the IFRS US$15,774.7m total revenue. The difference is the vendor's reclassification after US$4,578.7m of interest and other financial expenses and US$4,204.9m of expected credit loss: US$15,774.7m − US$4,578.7m − US$4,204.9m = US$6,991.1m. It is a presentation difference, not a second segment. [Capital IQ Financials→Segments, revenues, 12 months ended 2025-12-31 — vendor export; FY2025 Form 20-F, Consolidated Statements of Income, F-6–F-7]

## 2. Cost Stack

| Margin / Cost Line | % of Revenue or Amount | Direction | Evidence | Margin Risk |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| NIM (management-defined, annualized) | 22.9% in Q2 2026; +180bp QoQ | Tailwind | Q2 NII was US$3.7bn; management attributed NIM expansion to earlier lending growth, more unsecured-loan mix, and deliberate risk expansions. [Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.7; Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 15] | High: a lower lending yield or weaker credit demand would reduce the spread. |
| Funding / interest expense | US$1,556.7m; 28.2% of IFRS revenue; deposits were US$1,187.5m of this expense | Neutral QoQ / Headwind YoY | The IFRS funding line rose 51.1% YoY, broadly matching the 50.3% revenue rise. Deposit cost was 88% of the local interbank rate, unchanged QoQ and 3 percentage points below a year earlier. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, p.5; Note 6, pp.14–15; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.7] | High: rate rises, deposit competition, or a deposit outflow can raise funding cost. |
| Expected credit loss (ECL) | US$1,482.2m; 26.9% of IFRS revenue | Tailwind QoQ / Headwind YoY | Reported Q2 ECL was 46.4% above Q2 2025 but below the H1-implied Q1 2026 US$1,718.0m (= US$3,200.2m H1 − US$1,482.2m Q2). Management's separate credit-cost measure fell QoQ and added 115bp to risk-adjusted NIM. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, p.5; Note 7, p.16; Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16; analyst calculation] | High: larger unsecured balances and deliberate risk expansion can raise future provisions. |
| Transactional expenses | US$127.8m; 2.3% of revenue | Headwind | Up 63.2% YoY. Payment/network costs were US$44.7m and rewards US$47.0m, versus US$14.2m and US$24.1m a year earlier. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 6, p.15] | Not assessable: the filing gives no cost sensitivity or supplier-spend share. |
| IFRS operating expenses, net of other income | US$1,105.6m; 20.1% of revenue | Headwind YoY | Up 65.6% YoY, faster than revenue; general and administrative expense was US$599.8m (+75.8%), customer support and operations US$226.2m (+40.1%), and marketing US$103.4m (+53.6%). [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, pp.5, 16] | Mid: spending on international expansion and timing of real-estate and marketing costs can move the ratio. |
| Share-based compensation | US$134.4m; 2.4% of revenue | Headwind | Up 33.5% YoY and included in operating expense. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, pp.16–18] | Low at the current run rate, but it is an operating expense and dilution-related cost. |
| Depreciation and amortization | US$42.4m; 0.8% of revenue | Headwind | Up 83.7% YoY from US$23.1m, but remains small against revenue. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, p.16] | Low near term; it can rise as the FY2025 capex increase is recognized. |

The Q2 filing reports payment-network costs, including Mastercard and other card-program fees, but does not disclose the spend share, contract terms, or a sensitivity. The company identifies Mastercard and some third parties as sole- or limited-source services, so an adverse rule or fee change is a real qualitative risk but its basis-point impact is not proven. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 6, p.15; FY2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D, pp.111–112]

## 3. NIM → Risk-Adjusted NIM → Operating-Efficiency Walk

| Margin Level | Latest | Prior Year | Change bps | Main Reason | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| NIM (annualized, management-defined) | 22.9% Q2 2026 | 18.8% Q2 2025 | +410 | The company does not publish a YoY NIM bridge. Its QoQ read attributes the latest rise to credit-book growth and more unsecured-loan mix. | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slides 15–16; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.7] |
| Risk-adjusted NIM (annualized, management-defined) | 12.4% Q2 2026 | 9.9% Q2 2025 | +250 | The YoY move is not decomposed. The disclosed QoQ bridge shows credit income and lower cost of credit, detailed in Sections 7–7a. | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slides 15–16] |
| Implied credit-cost rate (NIM − risk-adjusted NIM) | 10.5% = 22.9% − 12.4% | 8.9% = 18.8% − 9.9% | +160 | The asset-denominated credit-cost rate was higher YoY even though Q2 cost of credit improved QoQ. This is a derived management-metric spread, not provisions divided by average loans. | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 15; analyst calculation] |
| Efficiency ratio (management-defined; not strict cost-to-income) | 19.5% Q2 2026 | 21.3% Q2 2025 | −180 | Lower ratio YoY, but Q1 2026's 17.6% was helped about two-thirds by temporary timing effects; Q2 operating expenses were US$806m, up 20% QoQ. | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 22; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.8] |

The management efficiency ratio and the IFRS operating-expense/revenue ratio are not interchangeable: the former uses a net-revenue denominator and an adjusted operating-expense scope, while the latter is US$1,105.6m / US$5,513.2m = 20.1% in Q2 2026 versus 18.2% a year earlier. The improved management efficiency ratio therefore does not erase the higher IFRS expense intensity; it measures a different basis. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, p.5; Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 22; analyst calculation]

Nu has no disclosed automatic cost pass-through and no measured realized recovery rate for a network, cloud, inflation, or other input-cost shock. It can adjust loan and deposit offers, but that is not evidence of broad customer-price pass-through. [FY2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D, pp.111–112, 136; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks and Q&A]

## 4. Margin Walk — Which Margin Level Matters Most?

Risk-adjusted NIM matters most. NIM alone rises when Nu adds higher-yield unsecured credit, but it does not deduct the associated credit cost. Risk-adjusted NIM therefore shows the trade between yield, funding cost, and defaults more directly; Q2's 12.4% result followed a 22.9% NIM but a 10.5% implied credit-cost rate. The efficiency ratio is a useful secondary gauge, but it is not a standard cost-to-income measure. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slides 15–16, 22]

**Cycle position: credit expansion, not proven peak.** The Q2 credit portfolio was US$39.4bn (+37% YoY), with unsecured lending up 45% to US$10.3bn; risk-adjusted NIM reached a company-reported high. This is an expansionary credit backdrop, but the available data does not establish a prior comparable peak, so it should not be treated as a normalized peak or trough. The Desenrola debt-renegotiation program was a one-time policy-related tailwind: management said it affected about 5% of Q2 cost of credit and that it was a minority of the 115bp contribution. It is not a run-rate margin source. [Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks and Q&A, pp.7–12]

## 5. Margin Driver Table (consolidated)

| Driver | Impact on Margins | Direction (Tailwind / Neutral / Headwind / Unknown) | Magnitude (High / Mid / Low) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prior-period credit growth and shift toward unsecured lending | Raises credit income and NIM, subject to later default costs | Tailwind | High | Added 178bp of the 294bp QoQ risk-adjusted-NIM rise; management linked it to cards, unsecured lending, and a higher loan-to-deposit ratio. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.7] |
| Credit cost, seasonality, and underlying payment performance | Lower cost of credit lifts risk-adjusted NIM; risk expansion can reverse it | Tailwind in Q2 / Headwind risk forward | High | Added 115bp QoQ. However, intentional risk expansion added 24bp to 15–90-day delinquencies and US$170m to the allowance bridge. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slides 16, 18; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, pp.7–8] |
| Deposit pricing and funding cost | Higher funding cost reduces NIM | Neutral | Low in Q2 | Funding cost contributed −5bp to Q2's risk-adjusted-NIM bridge; deposit cost was 88% of local interbank rates, 3 percentage points lower YoY. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slides 14, 16] |
| Float income and interest rates | Earned yield on cash and investments can move NIM | Neutral | Low in Q2 | Float income contributed +5bp QoQ. Rate sensitivity is material but the filings provide no earnings sensitivity. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16; H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 32, p.42] |
| Operating spending and timing | Higher expenses raise the efficiency ratio | Neutral | Mid | Real-estate and marketing costs shifted into Q2; management expects a full-year efficiency ratio of about 20%, not Q1's 17.6%. [Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.8] |
| Payment-network, rewards, and transaction costs | Reduces fee economics and gross profit | Headwind | Not assessable | Transactional expense rose 63.2% YoY; payments/network cost and rewards both increased. No vendor cost sensitivity is disclosed. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 6, p.15] |
| FX translation | Changes reported U.S.-dollar earnings and some operating costs | Unknown | Not assessable | Operating entities use BRL, MXN, and COP; the company hedges specified exposures but does not disclose a group earnings-margin sensitivity. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Notes 2, 20 and 32, pp.12–13, 27–30, 42] |

## 6. Margin Drivers By Segment (if applicable)

Not applicable. Nu Group is the sole reportable segment. Country and product profit margins are not disclosed, so a Brazil/Mexico/Colombia or product margin table would be a guess. [FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 34, F-97–F-98]

## 7. Margin Bridge — Latest Period

Nu provides a company-defined, annualized risk-adjusted-NIM bridge for Q1 to Q2 2026. It is the appropriate bank overlay bridge; the company does not disclose an IFRS gross-margin bridge or an exact price/volume decomposition.

| Component | Margin Impact (bps) | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Credit income from earlier loan growth and mix | +178 | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.7] |
| Lower cost of credit | +115 | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p.7] |
| Float income | +5 | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16] |
| Funding cost | −5 | [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16] |
| Other / rounding residual | +1 | Residual calculated below; no causal attribution. |
| **Total risk-adjusted-NIM change** | **+294** | 12.42% Q2 2026 − 9.48% Q1 2026. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16] |

## 7a. Bridge Attribution and Residual (MODULE_RULES "Driver Attribution" / §15)

All four named components are **asserted from Nu's disclosed management bridge, no sensitivity applied**. Their basis is the same company-defined, annualized risk-adjusted NIM for Q1 and Q2 2026; they are not applied to IFRS revenue, a different period, or a country/product subsegment.

```text
Credit income: asserted +178bp from management's Q1-to-Q2 risk-adjusted-NIM bridge; no sensitivity applied
  = +178bp of the +294bp observed change
  → basis matches: company-defined, annualized consolidated risk-adjusted NIM

Cost of credit: asserted +115bp from the same bridge; no sensitivity applied
  = +115bp of the +294bp observed change
  → basis matches

Float income: asserted +5bp from the same bridge; no sensitivity applied
  = +5bp of the +294bp observed change
  → basis matches

Funding cost: asserted −5bp from the same bridge; no sensitivity applied
  = −5bp of the +294bp observed change
  → basis matches
```

Reconciliation: **178 + 115 + 5 − 5 + 1 = 294bp reconciled, 1bp residual.** Credit income explains 178 / 294 = **60.5%** of the movement, so it clears the threshold for the single-biggest-driver read in Section 8. Lower cost of credit explains 39.1%. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slide 16; analyst calculation]

## 8. The Single Biggest Margin Driver

**Credit income from prior loan growth and the move toward unsecured lending is the single biggest current margin driver.** It added 178bp, or 60.5%, of the 294bp QoQ rise in risk-adjusted NIM, compared with 115bp from lower credit cost. Its current direction is a tailwind. The adverse counterpart is material: management's intentional risk expansion added 24bp to early delinquency and US$170m to the allowance build, so the same mix that raises credit income can later raise ECL. The Q2 bridge is well reconciled, but it is a single-quarter management measure, not proof that this spread is permanent. [Q2 2026 Earnings Deck, slides 16, 18; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, pp.7–8]

## 9. Investment Spend — Both Signs

FY2025 PP&E plus intangible capex was US$340.8m, up from US$175.0m in FY2024. That meets the higher-than-history test. [FY2025 Form 20-F, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, F-14–F-15]

| Reading | What it would show | Evidence here |
|---|---|---|
| Spend as a future COST | Higher depreciation and amortization as prior capex is recognized, which increases operating expense. | H1 2026 depreciation and amortization was US$76.7m, up 72.9% YoY; Q2 was US$42.4m, up 83.7% YoY. [H1 FY2026 Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, p.16] |
| Spend as a DEMAND signal | Backlog, contracted revenue, or capacity sold before it is built would show that incremental spend reflects demand rather than just cost. | Q2 credit portfolio growth was 37% YoY and net revenues reached US$4.1bn, but Nu discloses no backlog, contracted lending revenue, or capacity-sold metric tying capex to demand. [Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, pp.6–8] |

**Current read:** the future-cost reading has the direct evidence, although D&A remains only 0.8% of Q2 IFRS revenue; a positive demand read is not proven from available data. The observable that would flip this read is a disclosed link showing a specific technology or capacity investment generating incremental credit income or net revenue faster than its associated D&A.

## 7. Bar Assessment

**Bar is high.** There is no formal revenue or GAAP-EPS guide from management to compare directly with the FQ3 consensus, but the consensus hurdle has risen after Q2: FQ3 revenue is up 7.0% versus three months ago, FY2026 revenue is up 4.4%, and FY2026 GAAP EPS is up US$0.02. [Capital IQ Estimates — Trends, FQ3 2026 and FY2026] Last-month breadth is also positive at 8 EPS increases and no cuts, plus 5 revenue increases against 2 cuts. [Capital IQ Estimates — Revisions, Last Month, FY2026]

The latest Q2 result was a GAAP-EPS beat, but the preceding Q1 result missed both revenue and EPS; this history does not neutralize the higher revised bar. [Capital IQ Estimates — Surprise, Fiscal Quarters, Q1–Q2 2026] Management's approximate 20% full-year efficiency-ratio objective and non-numeric risk-adjusted-NIM commentary do not establish that the revenue or EPS consensus is achievable. [Q2 2026 earnings call, prepared remarks and Q&A, 2026-08-13, pp.8–11]

# Beat / Miss Setup — NU

## 1. Next Reporting Period Context

Nu is expected to file FQ3 2026, the standalone three months ending 30 September 2026, on 12 November 2026; the date is a Capital IQ calendar field, not a company commitment. **FQ3 standalone bar = FQ3 standalone vendor estimate: US$5,936.74m revenue and US$0.22164 GAAP EPS. No addition is required.** The bar implies 42.3% revenue growth and 39.0% EPS growth versus Q3 2025 on the same standalone-quarter basis. [Capital IQ Estimates — Consensus, Fiscal Quarters and current fiscal-year header, FQ3 2026; Capital IQ Estimates — Surprise, Fiscal Quarters, Q3 2025]

The available record does not support a three-year, like-for-like Q3 seasonality conclusion. The Q3 revenue bar has risen 7.0% in 90 days, and Nu gives no numeric revenue or EPS guidance against which to test it. [Capital IQ Estimates — Trends, FQ3 2026; Q2 2026 earnings call, Q&A, 2026-08-13, pp. 8–11]

Likelihood labels below are judgment based on the cited current drivers, not empirical probabilities; the four-quarter surprise history is too small to measure a repeatable beat rate.

## 2. Beat Scenarios

| Scenario | Driver | What Would Need To Happen | Likelihood (High / Mid / Low) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prior credit growth converts into Q3 interest income | Card and loan balances / realization | The Q2 portfolio growth must continue to flow through to credit-card and loan interest, keeping reported revenue above the US$5,936.74m FQ3 bar despite normalising originations. | Mid — judgment: the income-recognition lag supports it, but management says origination growth is normalising. | Q2 portfolio was US$39.4bn, +37% YoY FX-neutral; cards, unsecured and secured loans rose 35%, 45% and 30%, and management said Q1 balance growth matured into Q2 income. [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slide 13; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks and Q&A, pp. 6, 9] |
| Higher-yield credit mix sustains net interest economics | Unsecured-lending mix / risk-adjusted NIM | The prior-period book and unsecured mix must keep credit income elevated while defaults do not reverse Q2's cost-of-credit improvement; that would support an EPS beat even if fee income merely tracks activity. | Mid — judgment: the disclosed Q2 bridge was favorable, but management said the Q2 level was not a floor. | Credit income added 178bp and lower credit cost 115bp to the 294bp Q1-to-Q2 rise in company-defined risk-adjusted NIM; Q2 risk-adjusted NIM was 12.4%. [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slide 16; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks and Q&A, pp. 7–11] |
| Expense timing remains contained | Operating efficiency / marketing and real estate spend | Q3 operating spending needs to avoid another material step-up, allowing the FY2026 efficiency ratio to remain near management's approximately 20% objective and leaving more revenue at the bottom line. | Low — judgment: the stated full-year objective gives a reference point, but Q2 operating expenses were already up 20% QoQ and management identifies timing-related costs. | Q2 efficiency ratio was 19.5%; management expects about 20% for FY2026, while Q2 operating expenses were US$806m, +20% QoQ, after real-estate and marketing costs shifted into the quarter. [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 6, 22; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks, p. 8] |

## 3. Miss Scenarios

| Scenario | Driver | What Would Need To Happen | Likelihood (High / Mid / Low) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue growth falls short of the raised hurdle | Credit-book growth, activity and ARPAC | Portfolio growth, customer activity or yield must slow enough that interest income and fees cannot deliver the 42.3% YoY revenue growth embedded in the FQ3 bar. | High — judgment: the bar rose 7.0% in 90 days, management gives no revenue guide, and the latest 37% portfolio growth is not itself enough to prove a 42.3% reported-revenue outcome. | FQ3 revenue consensus is US$5,936.74m, +42.3% YoY; the 90-day estimate rose from US$5,545.80m. Management says Q2 originations are normalising after unusually fast growth. [Capital IQ Estimates — Consensus and Trends, FQ3 2026; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Q&A, p. 9] |
| Credit costs reverse the Q2 margin help | Risk expansion / expected credit loss (ECL) | Early delinquencies or allowance additions must rise enough to offset the Q2 cost-of-credit improvement, producing an EPS miss even if revenue meets the bar. | Mid — judgment: intentional risk expansion already affected early delinquency and allowances, but no Q3 ECL forecast or sensitivity is disclosed. | Intentional risk expansion added 24bp to 15–90-day delinquencies and US$170m to the allowance bridge; Q2 ECL was US$1,482.2m, +46.4% YoY. [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 16, 18; H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 7, p. 16] |
| Costs outrun revenue | Transaction, network, rewards and operating expense | Payment-network, rewards, marketing or support costs must grow faster than the revenue that the higher activity produces, eroding GAAP EPS. | Mid — judgment: Q2 cost growth was faster than revenue in several lines, while supplier-cost pass-through is not measured. | Transactional expenses rose 63.2% YoY and IFRS operating expenses net of other income rose 65.6% YoY, versus 50.3% IFRS revenue growth. Mastercard terms and network fees are a disclosed qualitative risk, but no cost sensitivity is available. [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, p. 5; Note 6, pp. 14–16; FY2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D, pp. 111–112] |

## 4. What Magnitude Matters?

The thresholds below are judgmental reporting-materiality markers, not forecasts or probabilities. They use the same standalone FQ3 basis as the consensus bar.

| Metric | Consensus / Bar | Material Beat Threshold | Material Miss Threshold | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Revenue | US$5,936.74m | >US$6,114.84m (+3.0%) | <US$5,758.64m (−3.0%) | A ±3% marker is judgment informed by the two recent revenue beats of +3.3% and +3.0%; it is not a measured likelihood. [Capital IQ Estimates — Consensus and Surprise, FQ3 2026; Q3–Q4 2025] |
| EBITDA / EBIT | N/A — Nu does not report EBITDA or EBIT, and the lender consensus export has no such series | Not assessable | Not assessable | An EBITDA/EBIT threshold would mix in a non-reported measure. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Income, F-6–F-7; Capital IQ Estimates — Consensus, current export] |
| GAAP EPS | US$0.22164 | >US$0.23272 (+5.0%) | <US$0.21056 (−5.0%) | A ±5% marker is judgment informed by the Q1 2026 EPS miss of −5.3%; the four-observation series is not a frequency estimate. [Capital IQ Estimates — Consensus and Surprise, FQ3 2026; Q1 2026] |
| Guidance | No numeric revenue, EPS or NIM guide; FY2026 efficiency ratio about 20% | Cannot define a quantitative beat threshold | Cannot define a quantitative miss threshold | Management has not set a numeric quarterly guide. A qualitative change in its NIM or efficiency commentary matters, but it cannot be sized faithfully against a missing guide. [Q2 2026 earnings call, prepared remarks and Q&A, 2026-08-13, pp. 8–11] |

## 5. In-Line Print But Bad Guidance Risk

| Risk | Evidence | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| In-line current quarter but guide-down | Management expects risk-adjusted NIM to remain in the same region as Q2, but explicitly said Q2 was not a floor; it gives no numeric revenue or EPS guide. [Q2 2026 earnings call, Q&A, 2026-08-13, pp. 10–11] | A result at the FQ3 consensus bar could still be read negatively if management lowers its view of spread or credit-cost durability. |
| Beat current quarter but weak margin guide | Q2 risk-adjusted-NIM improvement included 115bp from lower cost of credit, while intentional risk expansion added 24bp to early delinquencies and US$170m to the allowance bridge. [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 16, 18] | The same higher-yield mix that helps current income can lead to higher provisions later; a revenue beat therefore would not, by itself, establish durable margin improvement. |
| Beat EPS due to temporary cost-of-credit or timing effects | Management says Q1's 17.6% efficiency ratio was helped about two-thirds by temporary timing effects; the Desenrola programme was a minority of Q2's cost-of-credit benefit and not a run-rate source. [Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks and Q&A, pp. 7–12] | A beat assisted by timing or a one-time policy effect would have lower quality than one generated by recurring customer activity and controlled costs. |
| Beat revenue while cash conversion weakens | H1 2026 CFO was US$(1.242)bn and filing-built TTM CFO was US$(1.382)bn despite rising income. For this deposit-taking lender, CFO and free cash flow (FCF, CFO less total capex) are affected by balance-sheet movements and are not distributable-cash measures. [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Statement of Cash Flows, p. 12; Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, F-14–F-15] | A conventional working-capital conclusion is not meaningful here, but a revenue beat does not resolve balance-sheet funding, lending and cash-flow quality questions. |

## 6. Seasonality Read

Seasonality neither helps nor hurts the FQ3 setup on the available evidence: the historical-financials review found insufficient like-for-like primary quarterly history for a three-year seasonality table. Management has described Q4 as seasonally higher for purchase volume and revenue, but that is a Q4 observation, not evidence that Q3 carries a seasonal advantage. [Historical Financials — NU, §5, 2026-08-30; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Q&A, p. 9]

## 7. Historical Pattern

The last four reported quarters show no stable beat signal. Revenue beat in Q3 2025 (+3.3%), Q4 2025 (+3.0%) and Q2 2026 (+0.6%), but missed in Q1 2026 (−1.8%); EPS beat in Q3 and Q2 but missed in Q4 and Q1. This is a four-observation descriptive record, so it should receive little weight and is not an empirical probability of an FQ3 beat or miss. [Capital IQ Estimates — Surprise, Fiscal Quarters, Q3 2025–Q2 2026]

## 8. Setup Verdict

**Setup favors miss.** The single most important factor is the raised revenue bar: it requires 42.3% YoY growth after the FQ3 estimate increased 7.0% in 90 days, without a numeric company guide, while management says originations are normalising. The biggest risk to this conclusion is that earlier credit growth and the unsecured mix continue to mature into interest income fast enough to exceed the bar despite that normalisation. [Capital IQ Estimates — Consensus and Trends, FQ3 2026; Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks and Q&A, pp. 6, 9]

## 9. Second-Quarter Look-Ahead

The FQ4 2026 setup may differ because management describes Q4 purchase volume and revenue as seasonally higher; that could help card-related activity, but it is not a quantified FQ4 earnings forecast. Visibility is otherwise limited: no FQ4 consensus bar is carried in the guidance-consensus output, and the durability of risk-adjusted NIM, credit cost and the approximately 20% FY2026 efficiency objective remains the key issue. [Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Q&A and prepared remarks, pp. 8–11]

## 10. Pre-Mortem

If this setup fails, the most likely error is treating normalising originations as an immediate slowdown in reported revenue when the existing credit book can still produce a delayed Q3 interest-income lift. The opposite error is also possible: reading the Q2 risk-adjusted-NIM bridge as durable despite the disclosed early-delinquency and allowance effects from intentional risk expansion. [Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, prepared remarks and Q&A, pp. 6–9; Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 16, 18]

# Earnings Quality — NU

Nu Holdings Ltd. reports under IFRS Accounting Standards in U.S. dollars and has a 31 December year-end. Amounts below are US$ millions unless stated otherwise. NU is a deposit-taking consumer lender, not an industrial company: changes in loans, credit-card receivables, securities, deposits and network payables drive cash from operating activities (CFO). Therefore, ordinary working-capital days and free cash flow (FCF, CFO less total capex) do not measure distributable cash in the usual way. NU does not report EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization), so a direct CFO/EBITDA cash-conversion test is not assessable. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Income and Cash Flows, F-6–F-7 and F-14–F-15]

## 1. EBITDA → CFO → FCF Bridge (3–5 years)

| Item | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Trend |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| EBITDA | N/A — not reported | N/A — not reported | N/A — not reported | N/A — not reported | N/A — not reported | Not assessable |
| Net operating balance-sheet change* | (3,720.0) | (1,850.7) | (4,705.4) | (7,391.3) | (11,078.7) | Cash outflow increasing |
| Tax paid | (52.3) | (297.1) | (612.4) | (1,262.5) | (1,641.7) | Increasing outflow |
| Interest paid | (9.1) | (30.9) | (82.9) | (88.1) | (92.3) | Increasing outflow |
| Other operating items — net income, non-cash reconciliation and interest received | 857.0 | 2,934.3 | 6,666.9 | 11,140.9 | 16,313.1 | Increasing |
| **CFO** | **(2,924.3)** | **755.6** | **1,266.2** | **2,399.0** | **3,500.5** | Positive FY2022–25 |
| Maintenance capex | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not assessable |
| Growth capex | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | Not assessable |
| Total capex — PP&E plus intangible assets | 28.5 | 114.3 | 177.0 | 175.0 | 340.8 | Increasing |
| **FCF (CFO − total capex)** | **(2,952.8)** | **641.3** | **1,089.2** | **2,224.1** | **3,159.7** | Positive FY2022–25 |
| **CFO / EBITDA %** | N/A — EBITDA not reported | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | Not assessable |

\*This is not conventional working capital. It is the cash-flow-statement total for securities, credit-card receivables, loans, other operating assets, central-bank deposits, customer deposits, network payables, deferred income and other liabilities. The FY2025 US$(11,078.7)m build is: securities US$(4,812.9)m + credit-card receivables US$(12,445.8)m + loans US$(10,306.9)m + central-bank deposits US$(2,749.8)m + other assets US$(828.6)m + other receivables US$406.3m + deposits US$12,861.3m + network payables US$4,132.4m + deferred income US$5.8m + other liabilities US$2,659.7m = US$(11,078.7)m. It is mainly balance-sheet funding and lending activity, not a receivables-collection measure. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2022, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, F-13–F-14; Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, F-14–F-15]

Capex split not disclosed — total capex used. FCF may understate true recurring free cash flow. For NU, it may also be a poor proxy for distributable cash because lending and deposit movements sit in CFO. The company defines annual capex as cash payments for property, plant and equipment and intangible assets. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Item 5.B, “Capital Expenditures”]

The latest filed half-year reverses the annual cash-flow direction: H1 FY2026 CFO was US$(1,242.0)m and total capex was US$100.5m, producing FCF of US$(1,342.5)m, versus CFO of US$3,640.0m and capex of US$152.9m in H1 FY2025. The filing-built TTM calculation is CFO = US$3,500.5m − US$3,640.0m − US$1,242.0m = US$(1,381.6)m; capex = US$340.8m − US$152.9m + US$100.5m = US$288.4m; FCF = US$(1,670.0)m. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, F-14–F-15; Nu Holdings Ltd., H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Statements of Cash Flows, p.12]

**Capital IQ sidecar reconciliation.** The deterministic sidecar reports LTM cash from operations of US$(10,304.8)m from `CIQ Financials→Cash Flow “Cash from Ops.” [LTM 12 months Jun-30-2026]`. That is US$8,923.2m below the filing-built US$(1,381.6)m TTM CFO above. The vendor workbook presentation cannot be reconciled to the filed cash-flow basis from the available evidence, so it is flagged rather than substituted; the filed statement is used under the source hierarchy. [Capital IQ Financials→Cash Flow, “Cash from Ops.”, LTM 12 months ended 30 June 2026 — vendor export; deterministic `ciq_facts.json`, read 2026-08-30]

## 2. Cash Conversion Assessment

The usual CFO/EBITDA threshold cannot be applied because NU reports neither EBITDA nor an EBITDA reconciliation. Annual CFO nevertheless rose from US$0.8bn in FY2022 to US$3.5bn in FY2025 while net income also rose, which is better evidence than a non-GAAP proxy. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Income and Cash Flows, F-6–F-7 and F-14–F-15]

The latest period is materially weaker: TTM CFO and FCF are negative on the filing-built basis. The H1 FY2026 deficit was driven by US$8.1bn of credit-card-receivable cash outflow, US$6.6bn of loan cash outflow and US$2.9bn of securities cash outflow, partly funded by US$3.4bn of deposits, US$1.9bn of network payables and US$2.0bn of other liabilities. This is a growth-and-funding mismatch within a lender’s cash-flow statement, not proof that reported income is fictitious; it does mean cash support for the current earnings run-rate is not established. [Nu Holdings Ltd., H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Statements of Cash Flows, p.12]

## 3. Working Capital Trends

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Direction | Risk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Receivable days (DSO) | N/A — no trade-receivables basis | N/A | N/A | Not assessable | Credit-card receivables and loans are interest-earning financial assets, not trade receivables for a revenue-days test |
| Inventory days (DIO) | N/A — financial-services business | N/A | N/A | Not assessable | No inventory/COGS basis disclosed |
| Payable days (DPO) | N/A — no trade-payables/COGS basis | N/A | N/A | Not assessable | Network payables and deposits are not supplier payables |
| Cash conversion cycle (DSO + DIO − DPO) | N/A | N/A | N/A | Not assessable | A conventional cycle would be a category error |

The requested formulas use average balances and revenue for DSO, and average inventories/payables and COGS for DIO/DPO. NU does not disclose the required trade-receivable, inventory, trade-payable or COGS bases. Its main FY2025 assets were credit-card receivables and loans, and its principal funding liability was deposits; substituting those balances into a retail working-capital cycle would misstate the result. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Financial Position, F-8–F-9; Note 13, “Credit card receivables”; Note 14, “Loans to customers”; Note 22, “Deposits”]

The lender-specific balance-sheet read is more useful. Net credit-card receivables plus loans rose from US$15.6bn at FY2023 to US$17.6bn at FY2024 and US$27.7bn at FY2025, while deposits rose from US$23.7bn to US$28.9bn and US$41.9bn, respectively. Deferred income also increased from US$68.4m to US$71.6m and US$77.5m; it is therefore not a declining contract-liability signal. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2024, Statement of Financial Position Data, “Credit card receivables,” “Loans to customers,” “Deposits” and “Deferred income”; Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Consolidated Statements of Financial Position, F-8–F-9; Note 26, “Deferred income,” F-76]

Credit-loss coverage is the key accrual monitor. On a matched point-in-time basis, total expected credit loss (ECL) was US$5,022.0m on US$32,666.7m gross card receivables plus loans at FY2025, or 15.37%. At 30 June 2026 it was US$6,642.3m on US$39,398.4m gross card receivables plus loans, or 16.86%: US$4,522.5m card ECL + US$2,119.8m loan ECL divided by US$25,961.1m gross card receivables + US$13,437.3m gross loans. The 149bp increase is a credit-risk warning, but it does not by itself show inadequate provisioning; the allowance has risen rather than been released. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Note 13, “Credit card receivables”; Note 14, “Loans to customers”; Nu Holdings Ltd., H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 13, “Credit card receivables”; Note 14, “Loans to customers”]

| Share-based compensation added back in Adjusted Net Income | 359.0 in FY2025 | Y | Mid | [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Item 5, “Adjusted Net Income (Loss)” reconciliation] |

The adjustment does not exceed 15% of FY2025 reported parent net income, but its main component is recurring share-based compensation: US$359.0m in FY2025 after US$408.2m in FY2024 and US$289.3m in FY2023. Removing a recurring employee cost makes Adjusted Net Income less representative of the full economic cost of earning reported income. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Item 5, “Adjusted Net Income (Loss)” reconciliation]

The H1 FY2026 book tax expense was US$258.1m on US$2,190.6m pre-tax income (11.8%), but current tax expense was US$1,249.1m and the US$991.0m deferred-tax benefit made up the difference. This does not establish an accounting error: the filing says deferred-tax balances are based on temporary differences and expected taxable income. It does make current-period net income less cash-backed than its headline tax line suggests. [Nu Holdings Ltd., H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Statements of Income, p.5; Note 30, “Income tax reconciliation,” p.37]

[Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Notes 13–14; Nu Holdings Ltd., H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Notes 13–14] |

RF-EQ-001 (rising accruals divergent from cash earnings)

The two triggered rows describe a lender-specific forensic mosaic: cash collection risk is carried by an ECL estimate and that estimate rose as CFO turned negative. They do not establish an accounting misstatement; annual CFO improved through FY2025 and standard trade-receivable and inventory tests do not apply.

## 8. Accounting Trap Checklist

| Trap | Triggered? (Y/N) | Evidence | Severity /100 *(higher = WORSE — inverted)* |

This is a lender risk, not proof of premature revenue recognition. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Note 4, “Revenue recognition”; Nu Holdings Ltd., H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Notes 13–14] | 60 |

## 9. Earnings Quality Score

**54/100 — Material concerns.** The main reasons are the filing-built TTM CFO/FCF reversal, the two-row lender-specific accrual flag, the US$991.0m H1 FY2026 deferred-tax benefit that suppresses book tax expense, and a recurring share-based-compensation add-back in Adjusted Net Income. Offsetting evidence is that annual CFO was positive and rising from FY2022 through FY2025, the FY2025 Adjusted Net Income uplift was 7.1% rather than above the 15% threshold, and no repeated restructuring charge or conventional working-capital anomaly is evidenced. Cash-flow data is available, so no partial-data score cap applies; the missing reported EBITDA prevents a direct CFO/EBITDA assessment.

## 10. The Single Biggest Quality Concern

The central risk is credit growth consuming cash while the credit-loss estimate rises. At 30 June 2026, gross card receivables plus loans were US$39.4bn and total ECL was US$6.64bn (16.86%), up from US$32.7bn and US$5.02bn (15.37%) at FY2025. In the same H1 period, CFO was US$(1.24)bn despite US$1.93bn of net income because cash outflows into credit-card receivables, loans and securities exceeded funding inflows. This does not prove earnings are overstated: NU records ECL before losses are realized and the higher allowance may be prudent. It does mean the durability of earnings depends on collections and credit performance rather than the FY2025 positive FCF headline. [Nu Holdings Ltd., Form 20-F, FY2025, Notes 13–14 and Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, F-14–F-15; Nu Holdings Ltd., H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Statements of Cash Flows, p.12; Notes 13–14]

## earnings / 07_earnings-sensitivity.md

_Source: `earnings/07_earnings-sensitivity.md`_

# Earnings Sensitivity — NU

Nu Holdings reports under IFRS Accounting Standards in US dollars. It does not report EBITDA. Where a filing permits a dollar impact below, it is therefore shown as an allowance, pre-tax-income, or financial-instrument fair-value measure and is never relabelled as EBITDA or EPS.

## 1. Variable Selection

The five variables below come from the High drivers in the revenue and margin tables: credit-book growth/yield, credit cost, and the consumer-credit/rates dependencies, plus the disclosed transaction-cost line. Interest rates and Brazilian consumer credit were also included from the business-model external-dependency review. AWS and Mastercard are named third parties, but their recent-relationship export covers only disclosed relationships and gives no spend, contractual rate, or concentration; it cannot support a quantified sensitivity. [business-model external-dependency, §§1–2, 2026-08-30; Capital IQ Suppliers/Customers export, retrieved 2026-08-30 — vendor export, scope notes]

## 2. Sensitivity Table

| Variable | Base Case | Move Basis | Bull Case | EPS/EBITDA Impact (bull) | Bear Case | EPS/EBITDA Impact (bear) | Mitigation assumed | Confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Macroeconomic scenario weighting / credit-loss allowance | Weighted-average ECL (expected credit-loss allowance) of US$6,642.313m at 30 Jun 2026; the actual upside/base/downside weights are not disclosed | Company-disclosed ECL under 100% weighting to each macro scenario | 100% upside: ECL US$6,223.554m, US$418.759m below weighted average | **+US$418.759m pre-tax-income bound**, or +US$0.0853 pre-tax per diluted-share equivalent. This is not EPS: timing of provisioning and tax are not disclosed. | 100% downside: ECL US$7,147.013m, US$504.700m above weighted average | **−US$504.700m pre-tax-income bound**, or −US$0.1028 pre-tax per diluted-share equivalent. This is not EPS. | 0% — bound: no extra underwriting, collections, repricing, recoveries, or tax benefit. The starting weighted ECL already embeds management's macro model; a realised offset is not computable from the pool. | High for allowance sensitivity; Low for any earnings translation | [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 3(a), p.15; Statement of Income and Note 9, pp.5–6] |
| Credit income from earlier lending growth and unsecured mix | Q2 2026 annualized risk-adjusted NIM 12.42%; the Q1-to-Q2 bridge attributes +178bp to credit income | Company-reported Q1-to-Q2 risk-adjusted-NIM bridge; historical observed move, not a forward coefficient | A further one-period +178bp contribution / persistence of the observed tailwind | Impact: not quantifiable. Risk-adjusted NIM is annualized and the filing does not disclose the average balance and tax basis needed to convert 178bp into earnings or EPS. | Reversal of the +178bp contribution | Impact: not quantifiable on the same basis | Existing underwriting, offer design and portfolio mix are embedded in the observed bridge; no separately measured realised offset is disclosed. | High for the 178bp bridge; Low for an earnings translation | [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slide 16; Q2 2026 Earnings Call transcript, prepared remarks, p.7] |
| Credit cost and payment performance | Q2 2026 risk-adjusted NIM 12.42%; lower cost of credit added +115bp QoQ. Intentional risk expansion added 24bp to 15–90-day delinquency and US$170m to the allowance bridge. | Company-reported Q1-to-Q2 risk-adjusted-NIM bridge; historical observed move, not a forward coefficient | The +115bp lower-credit-cost contribution persists for one period | Impact: not quantifiable. The 115bp is a management RANIM bridge component, not a disclosed dollar earnings coefficient. | Full reversal of the +115bp contribution | Impact: not quantifiable on the same basis | 0% — bound: no incremental tightening, collections or pricing response. The filing does not permit a realised recovery-rate calculation. | High for the bridge; Low for an earnings translation | [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 16 and 18; Q2 2026 Earnings Call transcript, prepared remarks, pp.7–8] |
| Payment-network, rewards and other transaction costs | Q2 2026 transactional expense US$127.816m | Historical observed Q2 YoY increase: US$127.816m − US$78.311m = US$49.505m | Return to the Q2 2025 cost level of US$78.311m | **+US$49.505m quarterly pre-tax cost-only bound**, or +US$0.0101 pre-tax per diluted-share equivalent; not EPS and it excludes any associated change in transaction revenue. | A further US$49.505m increase, to US$177.321m | **−US$49.505m quarterly pre-tax cost-only bound**, or −US$0.0101 pre-tax per diluted-share equivalent; not EPS. | 0% — bound: no supplier repricing, rewards redesign, or customer-price response. The filing gives no spend share or realised offset. | Medium for the historical cost movement; Low for a stand-alone earnings effect | [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 6(d), p.15; Note 9, p.6] |
| Parallel interest-rate curves / funding and investment book | Whole-position, post-hedge DV01: a +1bp parallel shift across the disclosed curves reduces fair value by US$1.282m: −US$0.685m BRL − US$0.125m TRY + US$0.002m US − US$0.059m MXN − US$0.415m COP | Company-disclosed 1bp parallel curve shift; the filing says the result is symmetric for up and down shocks | −1bp parallel shift | **+US$1.282m financial-instrument fair value.** It is not an EPS/EBITDA forecast. | +1bp parallel shift | **−US$1.282m financial-instrument fair value.** It is not an EPS/EBITDA forecast. | Disclosed derivative hedges are already reflected in the whole-position DV01; no additional management response is assumed and a separate realised offset is not computable. | High | [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 32, p.42] |

Pre-tax per-share equivalents use H1 FY2026 diluted weighted-average shares of 4,908.841m: US$418.759m / 4,908.841m = US$0.0853; US$504.700m / 4,908.841m = US$0.1028; US$49.505m / 4,908.841m = US$0.0101. They are bounds, not reported or forecast EPS, because the filing does not disclose the tax and recognition-timing effects. [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 9, p.6]

## 3. Sensitivity Ranking

No same-basis dollar earnings ranking is available: Nu discloses no EBITDA and no earnings-per-bp, earnings-per-credit-loss, or earnings-per-transaction-cost coefficient. Rank 1 is the only company-disclosed allowance-dollar range; ranks 2–5 are ordered by the size and directness of their reported driver measures, not by an invented common-dollar conversion.

| Rank | Variable | Absolute Impact (avg of bull + bear) | Direction of Current Trend |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Macroeconomic scenario weighting / credit-loss allowance | US$461.730m mean absolute ECL change: (US$418.759m + US$504.700m) / 2. This is an allowance metric, not a forecast earnings impact. | Mixed: Q2 ECL was 46.4% above Q2 2025, while lower cost of credit helped QoQ risk-adjusted NIM. |
| 2 | Credit income from earlier lending growth and unsecured mix | Not quantifiable in dollars; +178bp reported risk-adjusted-NIM contribution QoQ. | Tailwind in Q2; portfolio growth and unsecured mix increased yield. |
| 3 | Credit cost and payment performance | Not quantifiable in dollars; +115bp reported risk-adjusted-NIM contribution QoQ, against higher early delinquency from risk expansion. | QoQ tailwind, but adverse-credit-risk direction remains visible. |
| 4 | Payment-network, rewards and other transaction costs | US$49.505m quarterly historical cost movement; cost-only, pre-tax bound. | Headwind: transactional expense rose 63.2% YoY. |
| 5 | Parallel interest-rate curves / funding and investment book | US$1.282m fair-value movement per 1bp simultaneous parallel curve shift; not an earnings amount. | Neutral in Q2 bridge: funding cost contributed −5bp and float income +5bp. |

## 4. The Single Highest-Sensitivity Variable

**Macroeconomic scenario weighting and the associated credit-loss allowance** is the largest disclosed range. It is mostly external: Brazilian consumer conditions, rates and employment affect borrowers' ability to pay, although underwriting and collections are company levers. The current read is mixed, not cleanly improving: the Q2 credit-cost bridge was favourable by 115bp QoQ, yet reported ECL was US$1.482bn, 46.4% above Q2 2025, and risk expansion raised early delinquency by 24bp. The adverse disclosed state is a 100% downside macro weighting, which raises the allowance by US$504.700m from its weighted-average level. It is a sensitivity, not a prediction of a downturn. [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Notes 3(a) and 7, pp.15–16; Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 16 and 18]

## 5. Interaction Effects

Credit-book growth, unsecured mix, yield and credit cost are not independent. The Q2 bridge assigns +178bp to credit income and +115bp to lower credit cost, while the same risk expansion raised early delinquency and the allowance; adding those two bps effects to the macro ECL range would double count related credit-cycle outcomes. Higher rates can also lift interest income while increasing funding cost, reducing credit demand and worsening defaults, so the disclosed DV01 must not be added to the credit-income or credit-cost rows. [Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 15–18; H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 32, p.42]

## 6. Non-Linear Or Asymmetric Risks

The credit-loss range is asymmetric around the current weighted allowance: the downside state adds US$504.700m while the upside state releases US$418.759m. That asymmetry follows the disclosed weighted starting point, whose scenario weights are not provided; it should not be extrapolated linearly. There is also operating leverage in the wrong direction for a credit shock: the revenue benefit from higher-yield unsecured lending arrives before the associated losses are fully known, while management already reported a 24bp rise in early delinquency from risk expansion. Transaction costs are also not a pure price shock: the US$49.505m historical movement can be accompanied by activity and fee-revenue changes, so its cost-only bounds cannot be added to a revenue case. [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 3(a), p.15; Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 16 and 18; H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 6(d), p.15]

## 7. Earnings Volatility Score

**68/100 — INVERTED: higher = worse.** Credit conditions, yield and funding all materially affect a lender whose disclosed downside macro allowance is US$504.700m above the weighted case, while the latest credit expansion also carries higher early delinquency. The score is below the extreme band because the filing discloses hedging and because an earnings-per-bp or earnings-per-credit-cost coefficient is not proven from available data. [H1 FY2026 Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, Notes 3(a) and 32, pp.15 and 42; Q2 2026 Earnings Presentation, slides 16 and 18]

| “Earnings accelerating” would overstate what the evidence proves | Triggered | Medium | Medium | Q2 reported growth and risk-adjusted NIM improved, but FY revenue growth had slowed, originations were normalising, management did not give numeric revenue or EPS guidance, and part of H1 net income came from deferred tax. Probability basis: judgment informed by the cited mixed evidence. [historical-financials output, §6]; [revenue-drivers output, §§4, 7]; [guidance-consensus output, §7]; [business-model red-flags-sweep output, §2] | The evidence supports a strong quarter, not a confirmed durable acceleration thesis. |

## 3. Red-Flag Summary Table

| # | Category | Red Flag | Status | Severity | Probability | One-Line Impact |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Margins | Q2 spread improvement is exposed to later credit losses from risk expansion and unsecured mix. | Triggered | High | Medium | Current yield can reverse into higher ECL. |
| 2 | Guidance / Consensus | Raised FQ3 bar needs 42.3% revenue growth and has no numeric company guide. | Triggered | High | High | The Street has already incorporated much of the Q2 strength. |
| 3 | Earnings Quality / Accounting | Credit growth consumed cash as ECL coverage rose. | Triggered | High | Medium | Current earnings lack established cash support. |
| 4 | Earnings Quality / Accounting | H1 net income depended on a US$991.046m deferred-tax benefit. | Triggered | High | High | Headline net income is less cash-backed than the book tax line implies. |
| 5 | Sensitivity / External Variables | Downside macro weighting raises ECL by US$504.700m from the weighted allowance. | Triggered | High | Medium | A consumer-credit shock can materially reduce earnings before any verified EPS translation. |
| 6 | Revenue | Credit interest and higher-risk mix drive the main revenue stream, with Brazil economically concentrated. | Triggered | Medium | Medium | Revenue and future provisions are exposed to the same consumer-credit conditions. |
| 7 | Margins | Transactional and operating costs grew faster than revenue. | Triggered | Medium | Medium | A revenue beat may not flow through to GAAP EPS. |
| 8 | Beat / Miss Setup | Beat conditions are more demanding than a miss against the revised bar. | Triggered | Medium | Medium | The setup favors miss, but that is judgment rather than a measured frequency. |
| 9 | Earnings Quality / Accounting | Adjusted Net Income excludes recurring share-based compensation. | Triggered | Medium | High | Adjusted framing understates the recurring employee cost. |
| 10 | Narrative / Framing | A durable acceleration claim is not yet proven. | Triggered | Medium | Medium | One favorable quarter should not be treated as a new run rate. |
| 11 | Historical Trend | Q2 acceleration conflicts with decelerating annual growth and incomplete seasonality evidence. | Unclear | Medium | Medium | The direction beyond Q2 remains unresolved. |
| 12 | Source Conflicts | CIQ and filing-built LTM CFO differ by US$8.923bn. | Unclear | Medium | Unknown | Filing cash flow governs; vendor-led cash metrics remain unusable. |

## 4. Red-Flag Score

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total flags triggered | 10 |
| Critical flags | 0 |
| High flags | 5 |
| Medium flags | 5 |
| Low flags | 0 |
| Unclear flags | 2 |
| Unavailable checks (data missing) | 3 |

The counts are category instances, not independent risks: several high-severity rows describe the same credit-cycle exposure from revenue, margin, cash-flow, and sensitivity angles.

## 5. Red-Flag Severity Verdict

**Material concerns**

The reported Q2 improvement is real, but its persistence is fragile: the FQ3 bar is higher after revisions, while higher-yield credit mix and deliberate risk expansion are already increasing early-delinquency and allowance indicators. The single most dangerous flag is a reversal in credit cost after the unsecured-credit expansion; a Q3 disclosure showing stable or improving early delinquency, ECL coverage, and cost of credit on the expanded book would resolve it. The deferred-tax benefit and negative lender cash flow add quality concerns but do not prove improper accounting or fictitious income.

## 6. What The Synthesis Agent Should Know

- 10 triggered category flags: 5 High and 5 Medium; 2 Unclear flags; 3 Unavailable checks. Several rows are overlapping views of one credit-cycle risk.
- Most dangerous flag: deliberate risk expansion added 24bp to early delinquency and US$170m to the allowance bridge while the credit mix drives current NIM and revenue. [Q2 2026 Earnings Call, prepared remarks, pp.7–8]
- Change the earnings verdict from any unqualified “accelerating” read to **Mixed earnings setup** unless the synthesis shows how FQ3 clears the 42.3% revenue bar with controlled ECL and costs.
- Apply the MODULE_RULES source-conflict cap: **Overall usefulness max 65** unless CIQ's LTM CFO definition is reconciled. The filing remains the authoritative cash-flow source. [earnings-quality output, §1]; [Earnings Module Rules, Score Cap Rules]
- Reconcile the business-model synthesis view that the annual/LTM CFO figures are not comparable with the earnings-quality view that the vendor LTM presentation itself remains unreconciled; do not silently use the CIQ cash-flow figure.
- Missing data: no numeric revenue/EPS guide, no three-year like-for-like quarterly seasonality record, no country/product P&L, and no verified EPS coefficient for credit cost or payment-network costs.
- The setup is dirtier than the headline Q2 revenue, EPS, and risk-adjusted-NIM results suggest because the same credit expansion supports current yield and raises future loss exposure.

## 7. Pre-Mortem — If The Earnings Setup Fails

The most likely failure mode is that the Q2 boost from earlier credit-book growth and higher-yield unsecured lending is treated as a lasting earnings step-up, but the same risk expansion later raises ECL faster than interest income and leaves the raised FQ3 consensus unmet. The warning is already visible in the 24bp early-delinquency effect and US$170m allowance-bridge contribution; Q3 like-for-like credit-cost and ECL coverage are the decisive checks. [Q2 2026 Earnings Call, prepared remarks, pp.7–8]

## competitive-intel — module synthesis

_Source: `competitive-intel/99_competitive-intel-synthesis.md`_

# Competitive-Intel Module — NU (Synthesis)

## Abstract

NU's pool contains no usable competitor call or permitted broker call-summary, so it has no real peer benchmark. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — NU, §§1–5, 2026-08-30] The net read-through for the standalone FQ3 2026 print is Not assessable; weight and direction confidence are also Not assessable. [Peer Read-Through — NU, §4, 2026-08-30] NU's demand, margin and market-share narrative is not testable against peers, so the gap is neither corroboration nor contradiction. [Narrative Triangulation — NU, §5, 2026-08-30] Eligible calls cover 0% of the single disclosed Group segment, leaving the full business outside the benchmark. Verdict: this module supplies no beat/miss or candor signal until peer calls enter NU's auditable pool.

## 1. Verdict Block

- **Net read-through direction:** **Not assessable** — no already-reported, scope-overlapping peer call exists in NU's auditable corpus. NU has a sourced FQ3 2026 consensus bar, but no peer signal speaks to it. [Peer Read-Through — NU, §§0–4, 2026-08-30]
- **Read-through weight:** **Not assessable** — when no eligible peer produces a read, an H/M/L weight is not assigned. [Competitive-Intel Module Rules, “Confidence and Weight are Two Different Axes” and “Score Caps”; Peer Read-Through — NU, §6, 2026-08-30]
- **Read-through direction confidence:** **Not assessable** — there is no direction to which a §10 probability band or basis can attach. [Peer Read-Through — NU, §§2–4, 2026-08-30]
- **Narrative triangulation verdict:** **Not testable** — the peer picture is empty, not negative. [Narrative Triangulation — NU, §§1–5, 2026-08-30]
- **Peer-coverage of subject /100:** **0/100** *(higher = more of NU's exposure covered)*.
- **Benchmark data-sufficiency /100:** **0/100** *(higher = better peer-call breadth and quality)*.
- **Dispersion:** **Not assessable** — zero eligible peer companies means no matched cohort or named outlier. [Peer Dimension Matrix — NU, §§1–2, 2026-08-30]
- **Single most important peer signal:** None available; Itaú Unibanco, Bradesco and Santander Brasil are named competitors, but each lacks a usable call in NU's pool. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — NU, §1, 2026-08-30]
- **Biggest contradiction or corroboration of the subject's narrative:** None identified because the cross-check could not be run; NU's claims remain untested rather than supported or refuted. [Narrative Triangulation — NU, §§2–5, 2026-08-30]

## 1B. Score Builds (reproducible — CLAUDE.md §12)

Neither score is inverted; higher means better coverage or sufficiency.

### Peer-coverage of subject /100

| Exposure row | Subject weight | Eligible peer coverage | Covered weight |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Nu Group — single reportable digital-retail-financial-services segment | 100% of disclosed segment revenue and profit | None: zero read-through-eligible, scope-overlapping peer calls | 0% |

Nu Group is the only reportable segment and represents 100% of disclosed segment revenue and profit. No eligible peer call speaks to any part of it. [Nu Holdings Ltd. FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 34, F-97; Segment Map — NU, §§1–2, 2026-08-30; Competitive-Intel Data Triage — NU, §2, 2026-08-30]

`covered_exposure_pct = 0%`; therefore `round(0) = 0/100`. The uncovered exposure is the full 100% of the disclosed Group segment, including Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. This score does not use Brazil's 91% share of a narrower geographic-revenue subtotal as though it were a share of consolidated IFRS revenue or profit. [Segment Map — NU, §§2–3, 2026-08-30]

### Benchmark data-sufficiency /100

| Component | Build | Points |
|---|---|---:|
| Reporting-peer breadth | N = 0 distinct eligible peers | 0/40 |
| Exposure coverage | `round(0% × 0.30)` | 0/30 |
| Source quality | No eligible verbatim transcript and no broker paraphrase | 0/20 |
| Peer-set provenance | Peer set inherited from `business-model/08_competitive-map.md` | 10/10 |
| **Pre-floor total** | `0 + 0 + 0 + 10` | **10/100** |
| **No-usable-call floor** | No verbatim transcript and no permitted broker paraphrase exists | **0/100 final** |

The provenance points show that the intended peer set was independently established; they cannot turn an absent call corpus into a benchmark. The whole-score floor therefore applies. [Competitive Map — NU, §2, 2026-08-30; Competitive-Intel Data Triage — NU, §§1 and 5, 2026-08-30; Competitive-Intel Synthesis Instructions, §1B]

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation (CLAUDE.md §8)

- **Strongest bear read-through:** Not assessable — no eligible peer management signal exists.
- **Strongest bull read-through:** Not assessable — no eligible peer management signal exists.
- **Single killer contradiction:** None identified; the peer cross-check was not run, so this is not evidence that no contradiction exists. [Narrative Triangulation — NU, §§2 and 5, 2026-08-30]
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** None from peer calls because none are in the corpus. Absence of evidence is not support for NU's narrative. [Peer Dimension Matrix — NU, §§1–3, 2026-08-30]
- **What data would change this conclusion:** `03_readthrough-to-subject` produced no peer-derived subject line-item confirmation or falsification boundary, so there is no boundary to carry upward. A contemporaneous Itaú, Bradesco or Santander Brasil management call covering all or part of July–September 2026 must first be routed into `data/NU/external/`; only then can a scope-matched NU line item, comparable and basis be set. A partial-window call would test only its covered sub-period. [Peer Read-Through — NU, §§4–5, 2026-08-30]
- **What would force a downgrade / rejection:** The peer contribution is already excluded. A future call that is historical only, covers a mismatched window, or barely overlaps NU's scope must not restore a current read-through; any future contradiction must remain an inference about NU until NU reports the matching line item. [Competitive-Intel Module Rules, G1–G3 and Timing Rule]

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| competitive-intel-triage | **Insufficient.** No verbatim competitor transcript or permitted broker call-summary is present. | Reporting peers cover 0% of NU's disclosed Group exposure; the full business lacks a peer-call vantage. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — NU, §§2 and 5, 2026-08-30] |
| peer-claim-extraction | **Insufficient — no usable competitor call in the pool.** | No management claim, quote or number can be extracted for Itaú, Bradesco or Santander Brasil. [Peer Claim Extraction — NU, “Per-Peer Claim Blocks,” 2026-08-30] |
| peer-dimension-matrix | **Consensus and dispersion Not assessable.** | The matrix has zero eligible peer columns, so every benchmark dimension and named outlier is Not assessable. [Peer Dimension Matrix — NU, §§1–2, 2026-08-30] |
| peer-readthrough-to-subject | **Not assessable — no already-reported peer with overlapping scope.** | A known NU consensus bar cannot convert an absent peer signal into a beat/miss read. [Peer Read-Through — NU, §§2 and 4, 2026-08-30] |
| peer-narrative-triangulation | **Not testable.** | NU's 37% FX-neutral credit-portfolio growth claim and 7% Brazilian consumer-and-SME profit-pool claim are neither corroborated nor contradicted by an eligible peer vantage. [NU Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, 13 Aug. 2026, prepared remarks, p.6; Q&A, p.10; Narrative Triangulation — NU, §5, 2026-08-30] |

## 3. Reconciliation

No material directional disagreement exists: the triage, extraction, matrix, read-through and triangulation specialists all find no usable peer-call benchmark. Two precision points require adjudication:

1. `00` and `03` sometimes describe the net peer weight as “zero.” Under the synthesis rule, **Read-through weight is Not assessable**, because a direction that is Not assessable has neither an H/M/L weight nor a probability band. “Zero” means no contribution to the master view; it is not a weight label.
2. Brazil's US$11,038m is 91% of the US$12,084m defined geographic-revenue subtotal in the deterministic vendor sidecar, but that subtotal is not NU's US$15,775m consolidated IFRS-revenue denominator and has no country-profit measure. It therefore cannot build the coverage score. The coverage calculation instead uses the 100% single reportable Group segment and zero eligible calls. [CIQ Financials→Segments (Geographic Segment → Revenues, latest annual column) — vendor export; Nu Holdings Ltd. FY2025 Form 20-F, Consolidated Statements of Income, F-7; Note 34(b), F-98]

### Five-Guardrail + Claim-Fidelity Pass

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| G1 — common calendar window | Pass: no peer window is compared with NU's standalone FQ3 2026 window; no absent call is mislabelled as a not-yet-reported peer. |
| G2 — inference stays inference | Pass: no peer inference about NU is made, and missing calls are not treated as a negative operating signal. |
| G3 — overlapping scope only | Pass: coverage is stated as 0%; no minority or mismatched vantage is made to speak for the Group. |
| G4 — ratios / FX / basis | Pass: no cross-peer absolute comparison is made; the geographic amount above keeps its U.S.-dollar and narrower-subtotal basis. |
| G5 — management only | Pass: no analyst assertion or broker verdict is carried; there is no call or permitted paraphrase to extract. |
| Claim fidelity | Pass: “Not testable” remains “Not testable,” not “contradicted”; the sourced subject bar is not laundered into a peer direction, and the geographic-subtotal qualifier is retained. |

## 4. Score Cap Application

| Cap Trigger | Applied? (Y/N) | Affected | Final Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| No peer transcripts | Y | read-through | Not assessable |
| Only one peer | N — zero peers | weight | — |
| No peer reported the window | Y | current read-through | Not assessable |
| Exposure uncovered (0% covered, below 30%) | Y | net weight | Low ceiling; superseded by Not assessable because no read exists |
| Peer set self-selected | N — inherited from competitive map | net weight | — |
| Broker-paraphrase only | N — no broker paraphrase exists | tone | — |

The deterministic exposure ceiling is Low because covered exposure is below 30%. The stronger no-eligible-peer rule controls the output: direction, weight and direction confidence are all **Not assessable**, so the Low ceiling must not be misreported as an assigned weight. [Competitive-Intel Module Rules, “Score Caps” and “Confidence and Weight are Two Different Axes”]

## 5. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Carry **no peer beat/miss direction** into the scenario view. Read-through weight is **Not assessable**, and direction confidence is **Not assessable**; there is no §10 band or empirical/judgment basis because there is no direction. The only decision-relevant signal is the missing peer-call corpus, not a positive or negative operating read. [Peer Read-Through — NU, §§2–4, 2026-08-30]
- Carry **no peer-derived falsifier** into §8. `03` adopted no NU line-item boundary, comparable or basis. Do not repurpose the standalone FQ3 consensus bar as a test of a peer inference that was never made. A routed peer call covering July–September 2026, followed by a scope-matched NU line-item boundary, is required before a peer kill criterion exists. [Peer Read-Through — NU, §5, 2026-08-30]
- Narrative verdict is **Not testable**. NU's 37% FX-neutral Q2 credit-portfolio growth and 7% Brazilian consumer-and-SME profit-pool statements have no eligible peer cross-check. Treat them as neither corroborated nor contradicted, and make no peer-based change to the governance/candor read. [Narrative Triangulation — NU, §§1–5, 2026-08-30]
- Peers cannot speak to **100% of NU's disclosed Group exposure** in this run. Brazil, Mexico and Colombia all remain outside the peer-call benchmark; do not turn a future view on one geography or product into a Group conclusion. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — NU, §2, 2026-08-30]
- Binding caps are the absence of any usable call and the absence of a comparable-window report. The 0% coverage band would cap weight at Low if a read existed, but here the proper carried result is Not assessable. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — NU, §4, 2026-08-30; Competitive-Intel Module Rules, “Score Caps”]

## 6. Simple Summary

- There are no real competitor calls in NU's auditable pool.
- The peers imply neither a beat nor a miss for FQ3 2026; no peer read exists.
- Weight and direction confidence are both Not assessable, not Low or “zero.”
- NU's demand, margin and market-share story was not tested against peer management commentary.
- The benchmark is blind to 100% of NU's disclosed Group exposure.
- Dispersion and a named outlier are impossible to assess with zero eligible peers.
- This module is useful only as a data-gap warning for the master; it adds no earnings or candor signal.

No competitor transcript or permitted broker call-summary is present in `data/NU/external/`; that directory is absent, and the subject-pool extraction manifest has no external source record. The competitive map anchors the intended listed Brazilian bank peers as Itaú Unibanco (BOVESPA: ITUB4), Banco Bradesco (BOVESPA: BBDC4), and Banco Santander (Brasil) (BOVESPA: SANB11). NU’s FY2025 Form 20-F names all three in Brazilian consumer credit, but none has a transcript in the subject pool; no sibling pool or transcript pointer for those tickers was found either. They are coverage gaps, not table rows or read-through evidence. [FY2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D, “Substantial and increasingly intense competition”; `analyses/NU_2026-08-30/business-model/08_competitive-map.md`; `data/` peer-pool inventory, reviewed 2026-08-30]

## 2. Coverage of the Subject's Exposure

Reporting peers cover **0% of NU's exposure for this run**: there is no usable competitor call, so no part of the single reportable Group can receive a current peer read-through. NU has one reportable digital-retail-financial-services segment, representing 100% of disclosed revenue and profit. [FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 34, F-97]

Brazil is the dominant uncovered economic exposure. The deterministic Capital IQ sidecar reports the FY2025 geographic-revenue subtotal as Brazil **US$11,038m (91%)**, Mexico US$808m (7%), and other countries US$237m (2%), total US$12,084m. [CIQ Financials→Segments (Geographic Segment → Revenues, latest annual column) — vendor export] The FY2025 Form 20-F's Note 34 geographic table matches those figures, but this is a defined-revenue subtotal rather than the US$15,775m consolidated IFRS-revenue denominator and has no country profit; it must not be treated as a 91% consolidated-revenue share. [FY2025 Form 20-F, Consolidated Statements of Income, F-7; Note 34(b), F-98]

Consequently, Brazilian retail credit, deposits, cards and payments—the area the three named banks would overlap—is uncovered, as are Mexico and Colombia. The relationships sidecar covers recently disclosed customers and suppliers only; its counterparties are not competitor transcripts and do not fill this gap. [Capital IQ Suppliers/Customers relationship graph, scope notes — vendor export]

## 4. Caps That Will Bind

## 5. Sufficiency Verdict

- **Verdict:** Insufficient
- **Reason:** The peer set and NU's next standalone reporting window are known, but there is no verbatim competitor transcript or permitted broker paraphrase in the subject's auditable external corpus.
- **Coverage of subject:** 0% of NU's disclosed Group exposure has a reporting-peer vantage in this run; the Brazil-led retail-credit core is therefore Not assessable from peer calls.
- **Active caps:**
  - Read-through and narrative triangulation are Not assessable.
  - Current-window read-through is Not assessable because no peer has a call to date-gate.
  - The net peer weight is zero; no inference about NU should be drawn from the three named peers' separate results disclosures without a transcript in `data/NU/external/`.
- **Critical gaps:**
  - Add verbatim or permitted broker-paraphrase calls for at least Itaú, Bradesco and Santander Brasil to `data/NU/external/`; peer-pool copies elsewhere would remain pointers, not citable evidence for this run.
  - The uncovered Brazilian core is 91% of NU's defined FY2025 geographic-revenue subtotal, but that subtotal is not a consolidated-revenue or profit weight; country-level profit exposure remains undisclosed.
